2. Plaintiff Mahmudur Rahman Mullick, since dead, filed the title suit against the appellant his wife for declaration that the plaintiff is the real owner of half of the properties described in schedule 'A' and owner of 14 83/194 annas share of the properties described in schedule 'B' to the plaint; and for a further declaration that the defendant (appellant) has no right, title, interest and possession in the said properties on the basis of the deeds taken in her name. The plaintiff made an alternative prayer for khas possession if he be found to be out of possession of the properties in suit. 

 30. Mr. M. H. Khondkar strenuously argued that in view of clear admission of the plaintiff in Title Suit No.163 and 183 of, 1949 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge; Alipore, West Bengal (India) in his written statement filed in Title Suit No. 183 of 1949 (Exhibit Z3 (1); in the petition of objection affirmed by his affidavit Exhibit Z2 (I) filed in Title Suit No. 163 of 1949 resisting the application for appointment of receiver (Exhibit) ZI(1); in the Solenama Exhibit P filed in Title Suit No. 163 of 1949. which formed part of the preliminary decree Exhibit O(1). and Final Decree Exhibit 0 made in Title Suit No. 163 of 1949; and in the written statement, filed in Title Suit No. 183 of 1949 wherein No. 207A, Park Street property was also included, 'the plaintiff is estopped from making any claim over the self-same property to have been acquired by him with his own fund and for his own benefit. To lend support to his argument the learned Advocate with reference to some of the evidence led by the defendant supporting her possession in the suit property submitted that in the absence of any evidence that the properties acquired by exchange were ever treated by the plaintiff as his own and 'he possessed' the same, the learned Subordinate Judge as well as the learned Judges of the High Court Division Clearly misdirected themselves in declaring the defendant as the benamdar of the plaintiff in respect of 8 annas share of the properties described in schedule 'A' to the plaint and 14 83/104 annas share of the properties described in schedule 'B' to the plaint; and confirming plaintiff's possession in' those properties other than the residence portion of 12, Farashganj Road, Dacca; and allowing joint possession in the said residence portion with the defendant. In this context the learned Advocate further submitted with reference to the application filed by the plaintiff in the First Appeal No. 140 of 1965 preferred by the defendant against the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court that the plaintiff's statement made therein clearly shows that the defendant has been in possession of the suit properties. The learned Advocate in elucidating this point argued that the plaintiff prayed for declaration of his ownership in the suit properties" and a negative declaration that the defendant has no possession therein; and in the alternative prayed for khas possession if he be found out of possession. In his evidence the plaintiff stated that the property (schedule 'B') "is still in my possession and on realisation of rents". By the decree plaintiff's possession in the 'A' and 'B' schedule properties other than" the residence portion of 12, "Farashganj Road ('A' schedule) was con- firmed, but about two years after filing of the First Appeal by the defendant against the said judgment and decree the plaintiff filed an application on February 14, 1967 before the High Court for appointment of a Receiver of the suit properties.
